tables.reason: Protected short-lived Drive/template reads and the bounded registration admission window share this namespaced store. Database constraints bound the internal history; the stable advisory lock still serializes all replicas. Disposable provider caches are cleared once, retiring legacy-key cleanup and its index.

Non-null JSON value and expiry; expiry index

tables.lifecycle: Provider cache values are encrypted/versioned and validated; expiry/malformed entries are purged. Registration history has a separate bounded namespace and one cross-replica admission lock; a cache miss never supplies authorization.

tables.reason: Retain the sole encrypted native issuer store for clients, consent intents, authorization codes, access and refresh credentials. Eliminate the obsolete permanent/nullable expiry contract and constrain purpose and HMAC identity at SQL boundaries. Keep spent refresh receipts until canonical expiry; never infer a missing effect or grant.

writers: NativeStateStore.put and promote_client under native quota/advisory transactions
tables.lifecycle: Encrypted per-purpose state preserves one-use code and refresh-family replay evidence through canonical expiry. Migration 0030 rejects incompatible rows atomically and rewrites no ciphertext.

Non-null ciphertext and expiry
Closed client/intent/code/access/refresh namespace CHECK
Lowercase 64-character HMAC CHECK

tables.reason: Durable execution, leases, checkpoints, dispatch and results for active document operations.
tables.currentChange: Production 0029 preserves five needs_review tasks, all input/checkpoint/resource/generation evidence and unique target ownership. This follow-up does not clear or replay held work. Task admission recovery for transforms and Smart Create shares one owner/kind/key-scoped projection without payload decryption, writes or new tables.
readers: PostgresTaskService get_for_owner/get_for_owner_bounded_result, kind-specific loaders, current-result and dispatch/recovery scans

writers: create_or_replay, claim, begin_smart_create, record_resource, save_document_transform_checkpoint, _owned_lease_update, cancel/discard_pending, _retain_expired_executions
constraints: Kind/status/evidence/checkpoint/attempt and lease CHECKs from migrations 0028/0029
Unique owner/kind/idempotency key
Live or needs_review in-place target exclusion
Lease-token/version/expiry CAS and transactional checkpoint generation
tables.lifecycle: Checkpoint before dispatch; ambiguous expired execution becomes needs_review and reserves its target. Duplicate events, worker races and cancellation cannot clear unknown side effects. All five known production review records and their original raw evidence are retained.

tables.reason: Current identity, encrypted Google credentials, refresh fencing, and per-user settings.
tables.currentChange: Migration 0027 clears access ciphertext without expiry (16 unusable values in production preflight), retaining refresh credentials and versions. Enforce access/expiry pairing, lease pairing, lease-refresh dependency and nonnegative fencing generations in PostgreSQL.
readers: GoogleAuthService._load_user/_find_identity_users/_resolve_identity_user/resolve_current_user
Google token manager and MCP principal/grant validation
PostgresExtrasService preferences/folder-icons/sort-order readers
writers: GoogleAuthService._upsert_user and sign-out/session revision changes
Google token manager _acquire_lease/_persist_refresh_response/_clear_lease
PostgresExtrasService atomic JSON/scalar preference merges
constraints: User primary key and unique Google/email identity
Access-token/expiry pair CHECK
Refresh lease owner/deadline pair CHECK
Nonnegative token generation and required token version
tables.lifecycle: Keep one identity and token-ownership row. Session revision revokes credentials; refresh leases use owner/deadline CAS. Consolidated principal preferences merge atomically so concurrent edits do not overwrite independent values.

retainedInputContracts.reason: The repository pins the exact historical validation contracts in immutable Git provenance and rejects deleting their owners. Their legacy QA input declarations remain inert; no QA resources or application paths consume them.

migrationVerificationExceptions.reason: One-time transactional data reshaping and disposable old-schema migration tests require direct database access. These exact exceptions are reviewed against the native SARJ020/SARJ429 guidance; no application query receives an allowance.

SARJ020.reason: Atomic per-user JSON map construction preserves all legacy icon/sort rows during the authorized schema migration.

SARJ429.reason: Seed the pre-migration schema and assert PostgreSQL constraints/data preservation before current ORM columns exist.

retainedSerializationCompatibility.reason: Old encrypted normal copy checkpoints contain null QA metadata. Discard only those null legacy keys when decoding; keep strict rejection of non-null retired QA payloads and every other unknown field. New checkpoints omit the retired keys.

migrationIsolation: Acquire the unchanged global registration advisory lock, then pause the old admission table and cache writes for the copy/drop transaction. Native OAuth state is preserved byte-for-byte; only replaced proxy collections and disposable provider caches are removed.
retiredCode: Unused generic OAuth SDK key/value and bulk API; active native state remains encrypted and permission checked.
Unused alias attribution columns, foreign keys, indexes and service injection.
Legacy disposable provider-cache cleanup branch and index.
